analysis:
Documentation-only PR. It adds DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS to the LaunchAgent passthrough table at docs/provider/cli-reference.md:1960. In docs/reference/configuration.md:685, 'Not forwarded to LaunchAgents' becomes 'Forwarded to the launchd provider job'. No source code or controls change here, so no regression is demonstrable from the supplied evidence.

Security relevance: the variable only toggles delta versus complete SSD checkpoint writes in the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041, TB-007). It does not change TTL, HMAC lookup naming, AAD, the KEK, account scoping, or the disk budget. A same-user process already controls the invoking shell and provider.toml, so forwarding adds no new boundary.

The patch excerpt's ordering looks inconsistent: the new row sits between the MiMo complete-prefix row and the MiMo wired-residency row. The intro text at cli-reference.md:1936-1943 still describes only DAILY_WRITE_GB and DISK_GB as forwarded, with no mention of INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS. This is a possible documentation inconsistency, not a security finding.

Unverified contract: I did not see LaunchAgent.swift, so I cannot confirm that passthroughEnvKeys or inferencePassthroughEnvKeys actually includes this key. If it does not, the docs overclaim. The consequence would be a misleading operator expectation, not a weakened control, because the default is on and a negative value only reverts to complete checkpoints.

Minor T-041 note: the threat model lists the at-rest posture unchanged. Delta checkpoints are described in ssd-kv-cache.md, which was not supplied, so I cannot verify that the delta format keeps the HMAC-only metadata and AAD invariants. That would belong to the code change that introduced deltas, not this doc change.
